trigger: During an async ADDREPLICA, one CoreAdmin REQUESTSTATUS poll from the Overseer to the target node fails with HTTP 503 while the core's registration is still running (held by a latch until it is unloaded); the Overseer reports the ADDREPLICA FAILED and releases the collection lock, and the client's follow-up DELETEREPLICA unloads the core mid-register.
reason: A single failed status poll is turned straight into STATUS=failed with no retry (OverseerCollectionMessageHandler.java:867-870), so ADDREPLICA is reported FAILED and the per-collection lock is released while the async CREATE/registration is still running on the node. A later collection operation (DELETEREPLICA) then overlaps the unfinished registration, which the Overseer's serialization is supposed to prevent, and register finds the core gone at ZkController.java:1325-1326. The triggers (one failed RPC, a slow registration, an ordinary client cleanup) are realistic. The consequences are an ADDREPLICA wrongly reported as failed (without cleanup it silently yields a working replica), an ERROR/DOWN publish, and an UNLOAD that cannot delete the core's instance dir (validate-1.log:2642). The check's own abort is benign; the defect is the premature FAILED and lock release it exposes, and it is recoverable by retrying.
summary: One lost REQUESTSTATUS poll makes the Overseer report ADDREPLICA FAILED and release the collection lock while the core is still being created, so a cleanup DELETEREPLICA races the registration (register aborts, instance dir is left behind).
